pages.title: Welcome to the demo
pages.content:
This is a demo: everything you create, change or delete here stays in this browser tab. Reload the page and the demo starts over.

You are **Anna Sonnenberg**. With Markus, Lena, Paul and Mia, Grandma Gisela and Grandpa Heinz, Aunt Sabine and Jonas, the au pair, you plan your days here.

children.title: Internet & Wi-Fi
children.content:
**Network:** Sonnenberg

The password is on the back of the router. Guests have their own network, *Sonnenberg Guest*.

Restart: unplug, wait ten seconds, plug back in. If that doesn't help: hotline 07231-00WXYZ99.

children.title: Restart the router
children.content:
From Dad – for when the internet is gone again. Read first, then pull.

## Check first

- [ ] Is it down on every device? If only one is acting up: switch Wi-Fi off and on there.
- [ ] Is the **Internet** light on the router red, or off?

## Restart

1. The router is in the hallway, in the cupboard under the coat rack.
2. Pull the **black** plug at the back – not the grey one, that's the phone.
3. Wait ten seconds. Really ten.
4. Plug it back in and touch nothing for five minutes. The lights blink for a while, that's normal.
5. Once **Internet** is green, all is well.

## If it still doesn't work

The hotline and the password are under {{page:wifi}}. And let me know.

pages.title: Recipes
pages.content: What we eat. A recipe puts its ingredients on the {{list:shopping}} with one tap. Everyone's favourites are {{page:spaetzle}} and {{page:pancakes}}.

children.title: Grandma's classics
children.content: Just like Grandma Gisela makes them — her {{page:pumpkin}} comes every autumn.

children.title: Cheese spätzle
children.content:
1. Beat the flour, eggs, a pinch of salt and about 150 ml of water into a sticky dough.
2. Scrape the dough into boiling salted water in batches, let it float up, lift it out.
3. Slice the onions into rings and fry them golden in butter.
4. Layer the spätzle with grated cheese and serve with the onions.

On cold days {{page:lentils}} goes well before it.

children.title: Lentil soup
children.content:
1. Clean and dice the vegetables.
2. Bring the lentils and vegetables to the boil in the stock and simmer for 40 minutes.
3. Add the sliced frankfurters and heat through.
4. Season with vinegar and salt.

children.title: Pumpkin soup
children.content:
1. Wash, deseed and dice the squash — no need to peel it.
2. Sweat the onion and ginger in a little oil, add the squash.
3. Pour in the stock and simmer for twenty minutes.
4. Add the coconut milk, blend until smooth and season with salt.

children.title: Quick meals
children.content: On the table in half an hour — good for busy days. Ingredients go on the {{list:shopping}}.

children.title: Pancakes
children.content:
1. Whisk the flour, milk, eggs, sugar and a pinch of salt until smooth and leave for ten minutes.
2. Heat a little oil in a pan, add a ladle of batter and cook both sides golden.
3. Serve with apple sauce.

children.title: Couscous salad
children.content:
1. Pour 300 ml of boiling salted water over the couscous, leave for five minutes, fluff it up.
2. Dice the vegetables, chop the parsley, crumble the feta.
3. Mix everything with lemon juice and oil and season.

children.title: Cakes & bakes
children.content: For Sundays and birthdays.

children.title: Banana bread
children.content:
1. Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
2. Mash the bananas and mix with the butter, sugar and eggs.
3. Fold in the flour and baking powder, and the nuts if you like.
4. Pour into a loaf tin and bake for an hour.

children.title: Plaited sweet bread
children.content:
1. Dissolve the yeast in lukewarm milk with a little sugar.
2. Knead with the flour, butter, the rest of the sugar and the egg into a smooth dough; leave to rise for an hour.
3. Divide into three strands, plait them, leave to rise for another 30 minutes.
4. Brush with milk, sprinkle with pearl sugar, bake at 180 °C for 30 minutes.
